what: Dev-only test of the both-gates blur gate (drishyam.agent JobConfig.blur_gate "both": imaging.quality refuses a view as blur only if its Laplacian variance is under SHARPNESS_MIN 12.0 AND its re-blur ratio imaging.reblur is above imaging.REBLUR_MAX) against the Laplacian gate as published, for the live v1 segmenter at the 30 % pixel cap. Never a held-out set. Pre-registration stub: the measure, the gate, its threshold and how it was set, the rule, the splits and the commands below were committed before any run of `python -m evals.blur_gate dev` was made or read; that run adds its numbers, clauses and verdict to this file, `python -m evals.blur_gate real01` then adds the real_01 report, and these fields are not changed then. This rule replaces the one committed in 1eea0bf, before any dev read (replaced_rule).
motivation: The quality gate refuses a view as blur when the Laplacian variance of its grey levels is under 12.0. That number is absolute: it scales with the square of the surface's contrast and falls with the pyramid level of a view of fine-grained texture, so it judges texture and contrast as much as focus. The team's wall photo real_01 (public/samples/real_01.jpg: sharp painted plaster with a hairline crack, no ground truth) has no candidate, so v1 takes its one whole-photo look at L2 (750 px, cause fallback-l2); that view's Laplacian variance is 5.1, the gate refuses it as blur although v1's mask there holds 9,135 crack px, and the work order gets a not-assessed entry with action re-shoot, an instruction that is wrong for a sharp photo (drishyam run --cost-model fixed --micro-arm local-macos-x86-dacl10k at a8aa8e0; drishyam/agent.py drops a refused look's findings and adds that entry). The judges' re-grade asked for a scale-free blur gate. real_01 is the motivation only, never evidence: no clause of the rule reads it.
prior_art: Crete-Roffet, F., Dolmiere, T., Ladret, P. and Nicolas, M. (2007). The blur effect: perception and estimation with a new no-reference perceptual blur metric. Proc. SPIE 6492, Human Vision and Electronic Imaging XII, 64920I. Re-blur the image with a strong low-pass filter along each axis and compare the variation between neighbouring pixels before and after: a sharp image loses much of it, a blurred one little.

scikit-image implements it as skimage.measure.blur_effect (h_size 11, the absolute Sobel derivative along each axis, a 2-px border, the larger of the two axes). imaging.reblur computes the same with OpenCV (cv2.blur, cv2.Sobel); scikit-image is not a dependency.

Why this measure: it is a ratio of gradient sums, so it does not move with the view's contrast (exactly, up to 8-bit rounding), and it reads blur against a fixed box in the view's own pixels, so a sharp surface reads alike at every pyramid level (tests/test_imaging.py: a scale-free dead-leaves scene at L0, L1 and L2 within 0.05, while its Laplacian variance spreads 2.9x; a quarter of the contrast moves it by under 0.02, while the Laplacian variance falls 16-fold). It is published and has a reference implementation to check against. A ratio of Laplacian or gradient energy across pyramid levels was the other candidate named; it has no reference implementation. Only this one measure was built and measured.

Why both gates: the Laplacian variance is what refuses a faint sharp view (real_01's kind), and the re-blur ratio is what can tell such a view from a blurred one, so the ratio is used only to take back a Laplacian refusal it contradicts. A view the Laplacian gate passes is never refused.
design: imaging.reblur(gray): for each axis, d = |Sobel along the axis| of the view and k = the same of the view box-blurred along that axis over REBLUR_SIZE = 11 px; B = 1 - sum(max(0, d - k)) / sum(d) inside a 2-px border; the larger B of the two axes. 0: sharp; 1: nothing a re-blur removes. A view with no gradient (sum d = 0) is 1.

imaging.quality(crop, gate): gate "laplacian" (the default) is the gate as published; "both" refuses a view as blur only if its Laplacian variance is under 12.0 and its re-blur ratio is above REBLUR_MAX, so it can only take back blur refusals the Laplacian gate makes. Glare and dark are tested first under both, unchanged, and every look still records its Laplacian variance as `sharpness`; under "both" quality() also returns the ratio (`reblur`), which each step's observation then records. An unknown gate name raises ValueError; the re-blur gate alone ("reblur", the replaced rule's design) was removed, not kept beside it (nothing else used it).

JobConfig.blur_gate (default "laplacian") is passed by drishyam.agent to imaging.quality on every look (only when it is not "laplacian": with the knob off the call is quality(crop), as before); it is a JobConfig field, not a profile value, so it applies to every profile alike. A refused look is handled as before (its findings dropped, a not-assessed entry with action re-shoot). Nothing else reads the knob: the MCP gaze tool and the router's overview keep the Laplacian gate. evals.harness.run_drishyam passes it like any JobConfig switch and records it in each job's `switches`.

Knob off is the code as it was: every line the knob adds to drishyam/agent.py and to imaging.quality ends in `# blur-gate`. tests/test_agent.py strips those lines and checks the agent's whole event stream on every bundled sample (classical engine) and three synthetic photos under v1's profile; tests/test_imaging.py does the same for quality() on 200 views of the bundled samples (L0-L3, five points each), and checks on sharp, faint, blurred and blown-out synthetic views that the both-gates gate refuses a view only for the Laplacian gate's reason. drishyam run's traces and work orders on the 10 bundled samples, and drishyam batch on them, with the classical engine and with v1 (DRISHYAM_ONNX), were captured before the change (a8aa8e0) and after it: byte-identical.

calibration.too_blurred_to_trust: A Gaussian blur of sigma 2.0 view px applied to the view crop (cv2.GaussianBlur(crop, (0, 0), 2.0)). A 1-px hairline keeps about a fifth of its contrast at that blur (peak 1 / (sqrt(2 pi) x 2) = 0.20), so a view blurred that much cannot be trusted to show the hairline cracks the agent zooms for.
calibration.pool: Outside every dev and held-out set, the same pool as the replaced rule's. 40 synthetic photos with damage (evals.synth.build_dataset, seed 5150, 2048 x 1536) and 20 without (clean, seed 5151; the demo photo bridge_08 that the clean builder appends is left out); the seeds used elsewhere in evals/ and results/ are 0-4, 7, 8, 11, 2536-2543, 4242-4244 and 9000, and a set's per-photo seeds are seed x 100000 + i, so no photo is shared. And 100 CODEBRIM photos in neither evals/codebrim_dev100.txt nor evals/codebrim_eval200.txt, drawn with seed 5150 (evals.codebrim.select_dev from the other 752 annotated photos). CODEBRIM has no bridge ids, so pool photos may show the same bridges as dev and held-out photos; they were read for the threshold only, and no label of theirs was used.
calibration.procedure: The replaced rule's procedure, applied to the both-gates gate (the owner's instruction of 2026-10-23). v1 runs on every pool photo as in the rule below with the Laplacian gate (evals.blur_gate.photo_task); every look is rendered again as its gate read it (evals.blur_gate.views: its recorded Laplacian variance must match) and scored as it is and blurred by sigma 2.0. REBLUR_MAX is the largest value on a 0.005 grid at which the both-gates gate refuses at least as many of the blurred pool views as the Laplacian gate does. Command: DRISHYAM_ONNX=models/drishyam_dacl10k.onnx python -m evals.blur_gate calibrate --workers 6 (views in runs/blur_gate/calibration.json, not committed; the 788 views are the first calibration's, view for view).
calibration.what_the_pool_shows: The Laplacian gate refuses 787 of the 788 blurred pool views (it passes one L1 view whose blurred variance is 20.0, which the both-gates gate passes too). Among the 787, the lowest re-blur ratio is 0.3711 (an L2 view of a CODEBRIM photo), so the both-gates gate matches them all at any REBLUR_MAX under it: 0.37 on the grid. At 0.37, of the 45 views the Laplacian gate refuses as blur as they are (16 photos, all CODEBRIM), it takes back 25 (11 photos; Laplacian variance 4.9-11.8, ratio 0.23-0.34) and keeps 20 (6 photos); both gates refuse the same 2 glare views. Whether the views taken back are sharp is not known: CODEBRIM holds some out-of-focus photos. The dev run alone decides.

rule: Stated before any run of evals.blur_gate dev. Agent: v1 (onnx:drishyam_dacl10k.onnx, the released weights c49416c10087...) at its own profile with v1-policy2 (agent.POLICY2), pixel cap 0.30, the zero-candidate fallback on (the default), governor overrides off (evals.harness.run_drishyam), on the fixed costs of results/local-macos-x86-dacl10k-retime/micro.json (the table v1's dev rows in results/dev/model_choice_dev.json and the zero-candidate fallback's rule were charged). Two arms on every dev photo: blur_gate "laplacian" (knob off, the reference) and "both" (REBLUR_MAX 0.37, as calibrated above); every job must record its arm's blur_gate and v1's profile. Splits: synth_dev (60), synth_clean_dev (30), CODEBRIM dev100: 190 photos, each split's dataset sha256 equal to results/dev/model_choice_dev.json's. (G) Gate accuracy, paired over the same views: every look of the knob-off jobs is rendered again as its gate read it (its recorded Laplacian variance must match) and scored by both gates as it is and blurred by sigma 2.0 view px. A view is refused if quality() fails it for any reason (glare and dark are tested first, alike in both gates, so only blur decisions differ). Per photo: its views, the views each gate refuses as they are, and blurred. Statistic: the both-gates gate's share of views refused minus the Laplacian gate's, pooled over the photos of a resample; paired 95 % bootstrap CI over the 190 photos (evals.harness.boot_ci: 1000 resamples, seed 0), once for the views as they are (G1) and once for their blurred copies (G2). G1 holds if its CI lies entirely below 0 (fewer views wrongly refused as they are); G2 holds if its CI includes 0 or lies above it (upper bound >= 0: not measurably fewer blurred copies refused). By construction the both-gates gate refuses a view only if the Laplacian gate refuses it, so neither G1's difference nor G2's can be above 0, on the whole split or on any resample: G2 holds exactly when its CI's upper bound is 0, and Harm can come only from G2's CI lying entirely below 0. Verdict on gate accuracy: Harm if G1's CI lies entirely above 0 or G2's entirely below 0; else Gain if G1 holds; else no measurable difference. (A) Agent level, both-gates arm against the Laplacian arm on the same photos (evals.dev_sweep.row's paired CIs, 1000 resamples, seed 0): (A1) recall at the 30 % cap is not lower on synth_dev: the recall ratio's CI (vs_ref_ci) has upper bound >= 1; (A2) the same on CODEBRIM dev100; (A3) clean false alarms are not higher on synth_clean_dev: the CI of the per-photo boxes difference (boxes_diff_vs_ref_ci) includes 0 or lies below it (lower bound <= 0), and (A4) so does the CI of the difference in the share of photos with any box (images_with_any_vs_ref_ci). A split on which the two arms' jobs are identical passes its agent clause trivially (CI [1, 1] or [0, 0]); the count of photos whose jobs differ is reported per split. Adoption: blur_gate "both" becomes the default only if the verdict is Gain and A1-A4 all hold. Otherwise the code stays behind the knob, default "laplacian". Decided on these dev splits only; real_01 is never read by it. If adopted, scoring it on a held-out set is a separate step for the owner to approve; nothing runs on held-out data in this test.
assumed: Views as they are are assumed sharp: G1 counts every refusal of a view as it is as a wrong one, so every refusal the both-gates gate takes back counts as a gain. That is not true of every view. synth_dev photos carry blur_region distractors (a strongly blurred patch hiding a crack: evals.synth.blur_region) and the generator's 0.7-px softness at L0, and some CODEBRIM photos are out of focus in places. The run reports how many views as they are the Laplacian gate refuses (gate rows), by level, and over synthetic blur regions, so how much G1 could gain, and how many of the refusals taken back may have been right, is visible beside the verdict.
known_limits: A measure that ignores contrast reads 8-bit steps and sensor noise as sharp: a faint surface blurred until its grain is gone can have its Laplacian refusal taken back (tests/test_imaging.py: concrete at a fifth of its contrast, blurred by sigma 8 L0 px and seen at L1, reads 0.30 at a Laplacian variance of 0.4, and the both-gates gate passes it). The sigma-2 copy blurs a view's noise along with it, which a camera out of focus does not, so G2 may flatter the both-gates gate on real out-of-focus views.

Sharp scenes of flat patches between clean edges read high: faint dead-leaves discs, flat between anti-aliased edges, read 0.41, above REBLUR_MAX, so their Laplacian refusal stands (tests/test_imaging.py).
REBLUR_MAX rests on the tail of the pool's blurred views: the lowest ratio among those the Laplacian gate refuses is 0.3711, the next 0.3804.
Blur is read in the gaze's own pixels; a fallback look's gaze is larger than 512 px (the long side / 4), which the net then reads shrunk to 512 px.
reported_not_in_rule: per split: the gate row (views; refusals as they are and blurred, per gate; the two differences with their paired CIs)
per split: refusals by level, and of views over synthetic blur_region distractors, as they are and blurred, per gate; the re-blur ratio's quartiles as they are and blurred

per split: the photos whose two jobs differ, and both arms' agent rows (recall, IoU-only recall, chance recall, boxes, critical boxes, needs-a-look and sign-off counts, modelled ms per job with ms_vs_ref_ci)

real_01 (python -m evals.blur_gate real01, run only after the verdict is committed, read by no clause): the photo loaded as `drishyam run` loads it (decoded, people blurred), under each gate: its whole-photo fallback-l2 look (level, gaze, Laplacian variance, re-blur ratio, gate result), the job's looks and those refused as blur, and what v1 drafts there: boxes by class, critical sign-offs, needs-a-look masks, status

replaced_rule.design: The re-blur gate alone: JobConfig.blur_gate "reblur" refused a view as blur when its re-blur ratio was above REBLUR_MAX 0.38, whatever its Laplacian variance; the clauses had the shape kept here (G1, G2, A1-A4, adoption only on a Gain with A1-A4 all holding).
replaced_rule.why_replaced: On the calibration pool, before any dev read, the re-blur gate at 0.38 (the threshold the same procedure gave it) refused 71 views as they are against the Laplacian gate's 47: 50 of those were refused by it alone (Laplacian variance 13-144), and 26 by the old gate alone (Laplacian variance 6.5-11.5, the faint-surface kind real_01 belongs to); 21 by both. So it traded the faint views it was built for against more refusals of others. The owner chose the both-gates design on 2026-10-23, before any dev photo was read: the re-blur ratio only takes back Laplacian refusals, so it cannot refuse a view the Laplacian gate passes.
replaced_rule.dev_read: none: evals.blur_gate dev never ran under the replaced rule; no dev or held-out photo was read by the replaced rule's code or this one before this file was committed

splits.clean: data/synth_clean_dev, 30 photos with no damage, seed 4243
splits.real: CODEBRIM dev100: evals/codebrim_dev100.txt in data/codebrim (none in eval200)
splits.check: each split's dataset sha256 (ground truth and images) must equal results/dev/model_choice_dev.json's datasets; the run refuses otherwise
